decision: Keep production settings and independent 4 KiB payloads. Larger SQLite pages eliminate payload overflow but do not improve the 256 MiB write median; random writes, WAL volume and aged metadata workloads regress. Retain candidates only as an isolated experiment.

selection_criteria.priority: Preserve independent-block random I/O and GC behavior while improving large writes.
selection_criteria.promotion: Only consider a default change if large-write improvement survives round variation and neither aged random I/O nor small-file/metadata performance shows a material regression; inspect space and WAL costs too.
selection_criteria.default_without_clear_win: Keep production settings, retain the experiment and state tradeoffs. No migration or external payload-store implementation in this experiment.

format_notes.latency_units: seconds; pooled call percentiles exclude final group fsync except small_file_fsync, which times create/write/fsync/close per file.
format_notes.page_usage: SQLite VFS and dbstat counters do not measure physical SSD traffic.

host_identity.sample_note: Read-only hardware identity during measurement; no settings changed.

validation.asan_ubsan: Not rerun; isolated page-layout experiment uses Release.

limitations: All variants explicitly use 2 MiB suggested cache per connection and a 16 MiB strict WAL trigger; the 4 KiB control is not the unchanged stock binary.
VFS-submitted bytes are not physical SSD traffic; OS caches remain enabled.
Shared host; all samples and stalls retained. No external filesystem rerun.
Aging is one deterministic 32 MiB single-block/alternating-deletion pattern, not long-running steady state; free-page and leaf-slack distributions differ by page size.
Read fixtures differ: FUSE 64 MiB, aged native 16 MiB; compare variants within each workload.
Page size changes apply only to new zero-page databases; no migration performed.
Space includes both live payload contents and allocated pages; freelist pages remain reusable.
